page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Configured with an x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 burstable vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at clock frequencies up to 3.9 GHz. It features 32 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. Advanced instruction extensions are available, including AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 matrices, and SHA/AES cryptographic accelerations.

The hardware configuration omits local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote block storage and general-purpose compute pipelines. Networking bandwidth operates at a baseline of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution, supported by a Geekbench single-core score of 2101, single-threaded gzip compression at 33.94 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 14.33 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded performance is tempered by the 2 physical core constraint, yielding average PassMark scores (8056.97) and lower-tier multi-core results in stress-ng (4316.26) and multi-threaded decompression tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the burstable flex tier offers economical access to high DDR5 memory density and advanced modern Intel instruction sets without requiring full, continuous compute core allocation. The instance yields stable memory throughput, clocking 7.58 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 8.44 GB/sec in static web serving. However, heavy compute sustained throughput, database execution, and medium-scale LLM inference show clear performance limitations. The r8i-flex.xlarge is tailored for memory-bound workloads with variable CPU utilization, such as in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, middle-tier microservices, and memory-intensive development environments.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance operating on the Nitro hypervisor with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked up to 3.9 GHz. It provides 4 burstable vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, complemented by 32.0 GB of DDR5 system memory at 7 GHz and a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance excludes bundled local disks and discrete hardware accelerators, maintaining a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX int8 enable strong single-core benchmarks, including a Geekbench single-core rating of 2101. However, multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-core physical footprint, resulting in bottom-quartile multi-core stress results and limited LLM generation speeds. Given its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and burstable processor model, this configuration provides balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy, bursty workloads including Redis in-memory caches, background batch processing, and caching web services.
